findings.title: Queries are now interpolated twice (runSplitQuery + DataSourceWithBackend.query)
findings.body: `runSplitQuery` now maps every target through `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters)`. The sub-requests built from these targets are executed with `datasource.runQuery(subRequest)`, which calls `super.query()` (DataSourceWithBackend.query), and that method already applies `applyTemplateVariables(q, request.scopedVars, request.filters)` to every target it sends to the backend. As a result each query is interpolated twice: `templateSrv.replace` runs over an already-substituted expression (so a variable whose value itself contains `$something`/`[[something]]` will be expanded a second time) and `addAdHocFilters` is applied a second time to an expression that already contains the ad hoc matchers, which is at best redundant LogQL parsing per sub-request and at worst produces duplicated label matchers in the selector. If interpolation must happen up front for partitioning/step calculation, the second pass should be avoided (e.g. by stripping scopedVars/filters from the sub-request or by only using the interpolated copies for partitioning decisions).

findings.title: Shard path re-interpolates already sharded expressions
findings.body: `runShardSplitQuery` interpolates the targets, `splitQueriesByStreamShard` then rewrites them with `interpolateShardingSelector()` (adding `__stream_shard__=~"..."` and `| drop __stream_shard__`) and hands the result to `runSplitQuery`, which (after this PR) interpolates them again, and `datasource.runQuery` interpolates a third time inside `DataSourceWithBackend.query`. So for every shard group the sharded expression is re-parsed and re-processed by `addAdHocFilters`/`templateSrv.replace` twice more. The new test assertion `expect(datasource.applyTemplateVariables).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(5)` (shardQuerySplitting.test.ts line 112) confirms this: one interpolation became five for a single query. Besides the wasted work, re-applying ad hoc filters and variable substitution to an already-interpolated, shard-annotated expression risks duplicated matchers and double expansion of variable values that contain `$`.

findings.title: New test asserts client-side interpolation of $__auto, which the real code must not do
findings.body: The test mocks `templateSrv.replace` with a blind string replacement (`input.replace('$__auto', '5m')`) and then asserts that the expression reaching `runQuery` is `count_over_time({a="b"}[5m])`. In the real `LokiDatasource.applyTemplateVariables`, `__auto`/`__interval`/`__interval_ms`/`__range*` are deliberately removed from the scoped vars so that they are interpolated on the backend with the *sub-request's* time range; a frontend interpolation of `$__auto` based on the full range would yield a wrong step/range for each split chunk. The test therefore validates behaviour that neither happens nor should happen in production and gives false confidence; it should instead cover a user-defined variable (e.g. `$step`) and explicitly assert that `$__auto` is left untouched.

findings.title: Assertion hard-codes redundant interpolation count
findings.body: `expect(datasource.applyTemplateVariables).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(5)` encodes the number of times the (now repeated) interpolation happens for a single query: once in `runShardSplitQuery` plus once per shard-group sub-request via `runSplitQuery`. This number has no functional meaning, is coupled to the number of shard groups produced by the mocked label values, and will break on unrelated changes to grouping/shard-size heuristics. Prefer asserting that the interpolated expression reaches `runQuery` (or that it is called at least once per target) instead of an exact call count that documents the redundant interpolation.
